factors.name: Size and parallel branching
factors.summary: Strong loadings of Number of empty sequence flows (0.92), Token split (0.84) and Size (0.82), plus Control flow complexity (0.72) and Connector Mismatch (0.71), suggest that larger nets in this dataset also have more parallel splits and more places inside parallel blocks. It is the dominant factor (37% of variance). Size also loads 0.53 on Factor 3 and Token split 0.46 on Factor 2, so the factor is not purely size.

factors.name: Connector degree and connectivity
factors.summary: Maximum connector degree (0.87) and Coefficient of network connectivity (0.79) define this factor, so it reflects how many arcs meet at nodes, both at the busiest connector and on average per node. Control flow complexity cross-loads here (0.60) and on Factor 1 (0.72), which fits its definition as a count of arcs leaving splits.

factors.name: Sparsity and separability
factors.summary: Density loads negatively (-0.79) and Separability positively (0.64), with a secondary loading of Size (0.53), so this factor describes sparser nets with fewer articulation points. Because the maximum possible arc count grows quadratically with the number of nodes, the negative Density loading may partly reflect size. Only two measures are assigned, Separability has a moderate communality (0.62), and the factor's eigenvalue (1.06) is barely above 1.

factors.name: Sequentiality (single measure)
factors.summary: This factor is carried almost entirely by Sequentiality (0.95), with no other loading above 0.18. It amounts to a single-measure factor rather than a shared dimension, and the near-1 communality of Sequentiality signals a possible Heywood case.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis (Bartlett's test significant, overall KMO 0.82), and the four varimax-rotated factors explain 85% of the variance. The structure is dominated by a size and parallel-branching factor, followed by a connector-degree/connectivity factor and a weaker factor contrasting Density with Separability. The fourth factor contains only Sequentiality and goes beyond the three factors suggested by the eigenvalues (the fourth eigenvalue is 0.53), so it is best read as that measure's own variance rather than a common dimension. Control flow complexity is the only formal cross-loading (Factors 1 and 2), and no measure is unassigned.
caveats: Four factors were extracted although three were suggested; the fourth eigenvalue is 0.53, so Factor 4 is weakly justified.
Sequentiality shows a possible Heywood case (uniqueness at most 0.005), which makes Factor 4 and its loading unreliable.
Control flow complexity cross-loads on Factors 1 and 2, and Size has a substantial secondary loading (0.53) on Factor 3, so the factors are not cleanly separated.
Connector Heterogeneity and Average connector degree were removed for low MSA, and Number of duplicate tasks was constant, so these aspects are not represented.
Maximum connector degree and Sequentiality have MSA values only modestly above the threshold (about 0.66).

The factors reflect shared variance among nets mostly produced by discovery algorithms and depend on this dataset, the varimax rotation and the chosen number of factors; they do not indicate causal relationships.
